label: copy-phase input u fed back early in the copy (first or second recalled position)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase on steps whose input is the letter u being fed back, and only at the start of the copy: recall_idx 1 (the input is orig(0), i.e. the sequence began with u; 85% of activation mass) or recall_idx 2 (u was orig(1); 15% of mass, weaker). It never fires on u in the original phase, on the delimiter, on any other token, or at recall_idx >= 3 (only 69 such steps). Magnitude is largest at recall_idx 1 with short sequences (top examples are L=4, u x 1 o <DEL> [u]). It gets weaker as L grows: activity is almost gone for L=9 and at absolute step t >= 9. Many recall_idx-2 u inputs in longer sequences are inactive, which is why the t <= 8 cutoff is needed.

issues: Factual claims check out on dev. All activation is in the copy phase, all on in_tok u, and none on the delimiter or in the original phase. Shares by recall_idx are 0.848 at 1 and 0.152 at 2; recall_idx 3 has only 69 actives and 0 mass. Mass falls off with L (L=9 share 0.001) and with t (t>=9 share 0.017).
Test score reproduced: P 0.961, R 0.902, F1 0.930, mass recall 0.983.

Misses (2033 test steps, 1.7% of mass) are almost all weak activations (<=0.22 relative) at step 9: L=8, recall_idx 1, where u = orig(0). This is a soft fall-off at the t cutoff, not a separate class.

False positives (761 test steps) are mostly recall_idx 2 at the boundary (t=8, L=6, e.g. 'r u 0 t y h <DEL> r [u]') plus a few at t=5-7. This is a soft threshold at the edge of the window, not a systematic token or history pattern. Conditioning recall_idx 2 on orig(0)==u gives nothing useful (recall 0.013).
Other variants did not beat the original predicate: t<=9 scored F1 0.898, L<=7 scored F1 0.878, and adding to_go>=1 scored F1 0.923.
Minor wording issue: the label's 'early in the copy' really means the first two recall positions within an absolute-time window, t<=8. The explanation states this correctly.
